title: RPO and RTO Planning for a Highly Available PostgreSQL Cluster
summary: How Recovery Point Objective (data-loss tolerance) and Recovery Time Objective (downtime tolerance) drive PostgreSQL architecture decisions, and how synchronous replication's quorum commit turns an RPO target into an enforceable guarantee.

references.label: Shaun Thomas, "PostgreSQL 12 High Availability Cookbook", 3rd Edition (Packt, 2020) — Chapter 1, "Architectural Considerations", p. 8-15
PostgreSQL Documentation — Synchronous Replication (synchronous_standby_names, quorum commit)
PostgreSQL 17 Release Notes — Incremental backup (pg_basebackup, pg_combinebackup)

title: PostgreSQL Node Count and Geographic Placement
summary: How to derive how many PostgreSQL nodes a highly available cluster needs (backup, replicas, witness) and where to place them across data centers, and how Patroni's DCS-based quorum has replaced the manually placed witness node.

references.label: Shaun Thomas, "PostgreSQL 12 High Availability Cookbook", 3rd Edition (Packt, 2020) — Chapter 1, "Architectural Considerations", recipes "Picking redundant copies" and "Selecting locations", p. 15-21
PostgreSQL Documentation — Synchronous Replication
PostgreSQL Documentation — High Availability, Load Balancing, and Replication
Patroni Documentation — Architecture and DCS-based quorum

title: PostgreSQL Quorum Voting and Connection Indirection
summary: How witness-node voting rules avoid tied elections during automated failover, and how connection indirection (DNS, VIP, connection multiplexer, or load balancer) keeps applications from needing reconfiguration when the primary changes — today typically HAProxy polling Patroni's own REST health-check API.

references.label: Shaun Thomas, "PostgreSQL 12 High Availability Cookbook", 3rd Edition (Packt, 2020) — Chapter 1, "Architectural Considerations", recipes "Considering quorum" and "Introducing indirection", p. 25-30
PostgreSQL Documentation — High Availability, Load Balancing, and Replication

title: PostgreSQL Split-Brain Prevention: Fencing, STONITH, and SMITH
summary: How fencing guarantees a demoted or isolated PostgreSQL primary genuinely can't accept writes anymore — STONITH (remote power-off) and SMITH (self-power-off on isolation) — and how Patroni's built-in watchdog now automates the SMITH half via a Linux softdog/hardware watchdog device instead of a hand-rolled isolation check.

references.label: Shaun Thomas, "PostgreSQL 12 High Availability Cookbook", 3rd Edition (Packt, 2020) — Chapter 1, "Architectural Considerations", recipe "Preventing split brain", p. 31-33
PostgreSQL Documentation — High Availability, Load Balancing, and Replication

Patroni Documentation — FAQ (Postgres must be managed exclusively by Patroni)

title: PostgreSQL Multi-Master Clusters: Latency, Mesh Overhead, and Zero-RTO Failover
summary: How multi-master PostgreSQL trades the failover/quorum problem for a write-conflict-avoidance problem, why mesh topology overhead grows as C = N*(N-1), and how the 2020 book's generic 'proprietary software' framing maps to today's EDB Postgres Distributed and the newly open-source pgEdge/Spock.

references.label: Shaun Thomas, "PostgreSQL 12 High Availability Cookbook", 3rd Edition (Packt, 2020) — Chapter 1, "Architectural Considerations", recipes "Incorporating multi-master" and "Leveraging multi-master", p. 34-41

PostgreSQL Documentation — Conflict Detection and Logging in Logical Replication

title: PostgreSQL SLA Design: Defining Acceptable Downtime
summary: How to translate 'who uses the database and what will they tolerate' into a concrete uptime target expressed in nines, and how the book's ad-hoc SLA checklist maps to today's formal SLI/SLO/SLA/error-budget vocabulary and published managed-Postgres SLA benchmarks (AWS RDS, Google Cloud SQL).

title: PostgreSQL Initial Configuration: Connections, Memory, WAL, and Planner Costs
summary: How to set a defensible starting postgresql.conf for a highly available server — connection/memory sizing, WAL and checkpoint tuning, replication readiness, planner cost estimates, and logging — and which of the book's specific settings were renamed, removed, or became the default since 2020 (wal_level's hot_standby→replica, wal_keep_segments→wal_keep_size, checkpoint_completion_target's default now 0.9).

title: Limiting and Randomly Sampling Query Results
summary: How PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQL Server each cap the number of rows a query returns (LIMIT, TOP, and the ANSI FETCH FIRST standard MySQL doesn't support), how to randomize the sample before capping it, and why TABLESAMPLE beats ORDER BY RANDOM() for large tables.

title: Handling NULLs and Pattern Matching in SQL
summary: How IS NULL/IS NOT NULL and COALESCE handle missing data portably across databases, how LIKE's % and _ wildcards match partial text, and the case-sensitivity and indexing gotchas (leading vs trailing wildcards, pg_trgm) that differ across PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQL Server.

title: Conditional Sorting: NULLs and Data-Dependent Order in SQL
summary: How to sort NULLs to a specific position independent of the non-NULL order, and how to sort by a key that depends on another column's value — and why the book's claim that PostgreSQL needs the same workaround as MySQL/SQL Server for NULL sorting is simply wrong (PostgreSQL has had native NULLS FIRST/LAST since 2008).

summary: How the pg_settings.context column tells you whether changing a setting needs a full postmaster restart, a SIGHUP reload, or a superuser/user-level SET, how IS DISTINCT FROM safely lists settings changed from their boot_val default, and how PostgreSQL 15's GRANT SET/ALTER SYSTEM ON PARAMETER now lets admins delegate specific superuser-context settings to non-superuser roles without a full superuser grant.

title: Stacking Rowsets: UNION, UNION ALL, and the Wider Set-Operator Family
summary: How UNION ALL vertically stacks rowsets and UNION does the same while deduplicating (at the cost of a sort), why column count and type compatibility rules are identical across PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQL Server, and how MySQL 8.0.31 (2022) closed its long-standing INTERSECT/EXCEPT gap — while SQL Server still has no ALL variant for either.

title: Finding Your Busiest Tables: Activity and Bloat Stats in PostgreSQL
summary: How to rank tables and indexes by size (pg_total_relation_size), by write/read activity (pg_stat_user_tables, pg_stat_user_indexes), and by bloat (the pgstattuple extension) — and how PostgreSQL 16's last_seq_scan/last_idx_scan columns solve the book's own complaint that activity counters have no associated timestamp.

title: Anti-Joins and Optional Joins: Finding Missing Rows and Adding Data Without Losing Rows
summary: How LEFT JOIN + IS NULL (an anti-join) finds rows in one table with no match in another, how the same LEFT JOIN mechanism — or a scalar subquery in the SELECT list — adds optional data to an already-correct query without dropping rows, and why MySQL and PostgreSQL both recognize the anti-join pattern and stop scanning early instead of evaluating it as a naive join-then-filter.
